item.research_question: What intrinsic factors control the brittle versus ductile nature of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs), specifically comparing the ductile TiZrHfNbTa and the brittle VNbMoTaW?
item.material_system: Equiatomic TiZrHfNbTa (containing 60 at% HCP elements) and VNbMoTaW (containing 0 at% HCP elements)
item.processing_route: Arc-melting constituent elements (>99.9% pure) in argon atmosphere; TiZrHfNbTa rolled 50% at room temperature and annealed at 1200 °C for 144 h followed by water quenching; VNbMoTaW annealed at ~2000 °C for 48 h in an optical floating-zone furnace in flowing Ar
item.test_conditions: Compression tests on polycrystalline specimens (2 × 2 × 5 mm³) in vacuum at temperatures 77–1073 K with strain rate 1 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; micropillar compression at room temperature with nominal strain rate 1 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹
key_findings: TiZrHfNbTa is ductile down to 77 K, whereas VNbMoTaW is brittle below 298 K.
The brittle-to-ductile transition temperature (BDTT) is 247 K for TiZrHfNbTa and 627 K for VNbMoTaW.
The shear modulus (G) is 28.8 GPa for TiZrHfNbTa and 74.0 GPa for VNbMoTaW.
The mean square atomic displacement (MSAD) normalized by Burgers vector exceeds 6% for TiZrHfNbTa, while VNbMoTaW is close to FCC HEAs.
Screw dislocations dominate the microstructure of TiZrHfNbTa, while edge and screw segments are present in roughly equal numbers in VNbMoTaW.
The preferred slip plane is (2¯11) for TiZrHfNbTa and (1¯01) for VNbMoTaW.
The dislocation core energy in TiZrHfNbTa is significantly lower than in VNbMoTaW.
The athermal stress (σμ) is 798 MPa for TiZrHfNbTa and 830 MPa for VNbMoTaW.
item.mechanism: The higher concentration of HCP elements in TiZrHfNbTa lowers the dislocation core energy, increases lattice distortion, and reduces the shear modulus relative to VNbMoTaW. The extended dislocation cores and lower core energy in TiZrHfNbTa facilitate easier dislocation nucleation and motion, leading to higher ductility and a lower BDTT, whereas the compact cores and high core energy in VNbMoTaW restrict plasticity.
item.limitations: First-principles calculations for dislocation motion were limited to binary virtual Nb-Zr alloys using the Virtual Crystal Approximation (VCA) rather than the actual quinary RHEAs due to computing limitations; short-range ordering and clustering were not explicitly investigated.
item.future_work: Further research employing more realistic compositions is needed for a more comprehensive understanding of dislocation motion in multi-component RHEAs.
quotes: The former is compressible to 77 K, whereas the latter is not below 298 K.
Hexagonal close-packed (HCP) elements in TiZrHfNbTa lower its dislocation core energy, increase lattice distortion, and lower its shear modulus relative to VNbMoTaW whose elements are all BCC.
Our findings demonstrate how ductility and strength can be controlled through the ratio of HCP to BCC elements in RHEAs.
